newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan June M2 money supply up 8.35 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan June M2 money supply up 8.35 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Taiwan's broadest money supply measure, M2, grew 8.35 percent in June compared to June 1996, the central bank said on Friday.

The year-on-year M2 increase in June fell outside the central bank's target zone of 9-14 percent growth for the second straight month after the central bank adopted a new, broader definition of M2 in January.

Analysts have said the new broader definition could be expected to add 1.0 to 1.5 percentage points to the closely watched indicator. Before the shift, it had been 16 months since M2 growth had hit target.
The June M2 growth was slightly below an average forecast of 8.66 percent complied from July 23 Reuters Poll of Taiwan economists.
M2 growth in May was a year-on-year 8.99 percent.
The central bank attributed the low June M2 money supply growth to slowing growth in bank loans and investments and a higher basis in 1996.
Bank loans and investments rose 5.87 percent year-on-year, lower than a 6.10 percent rise in May and was the lowest since March 1987, the central bank said.

Economists have said they expected slow M2 growth in June, reflecting foreign fund outflows and the central bank's tightening of liquidity through repeated issuance of negotiable certificates of deposit and treasury bills to cool the red-hot stock market.
